items.title: The Balance Within: A Motivational Theory of Emotional Intelligence and Resilience
items.abstract: The Balance Within offers an insightful journey into the intricate relationship between emotional intelligence and resilience, exploring how motivation rooted in emotional awareness cultivates inner strength. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad presents a compelling theory that underscores the dynamic interplay between understanding one’s emotions and developing the capacity to bounce back from adversity. This book delves into the psychological and emotional mechanisms that empower individuals to maintain equilibrium amid life's challenges, promoting growth, well-being, and adaptive success. This work expands the boundaries of emotional intelligence research by integrating motivation as a critical driver for resilience, revealing practical approaches to nurture this balance within. Through thoughtful analysis and real-world examples, Rachmad provides a transformative framework that equips readers to harness emotional insights as a foundation for enduring personal and professional resilience. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad wrote this book in 1997, inspired by the growing recognition that resilience is not merely an innate trait but a skill deeply connected to emotional intelligence and motivation. Published by UNICEF, this work reflects a commitment to fostering resilient individuals capable of navigating increasingly complex social and emotional landscapes. At the heart of this theory lies emotional intelligence—defined as the ability to perceive, understand, and manage emotions—and resilience, described as the capacity to recover and thrive following setbacks. Motivation acts as the energizing force that bridges emotional insight with resilient behavior. Rachmad observed that individuals with high emotional awareness often demonstrate stronger resilience, but only when motivated by meaningful goals and internal drive. This linkage forms the basis for understanding how emotional intelligence and motivation coalesce to foster lasting psychological strength. The theory operates on the principle that cultivating emotional intelligence enhances motivation, which in turn reinforces resilience, creating a self-sustaining cycle of growth and adaptation. Key indicators include emotional regulation under stress, proactive problem-solving, optimistic outlooks, and the ability to learn from adversity. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad presents a theory that positions thoughtful reflection, critical analysis, and intentional cognitive effort as the sparks igniting breakthrough achievements. Moving beyond superficial learning, this work highlights how sustained intellectual rigor fosters innovation, problem-solving mastery, and adaptive success in a complex world. Rachmad articulates how nurturing deep thinking not only amplifies intellectual capacity but also serves as a dynamic force empowering individuals to navigate challenges, seize opportunities, and realize their fullest potential. Through practical insights and illustrative cases, readers are guided to embrace the power of concentrated thought as a driver for meaningful change across all life domains. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad wrote this book in 1997 under the auspices of UNICEF, inspired by the emerging recognition that intellectual growth is most potent when rooted in deliberate, focused thinking. The author sought to bridge academic concepts with actionable strategies to help individuals leverage deep cognitive processes for breakthrough development. At the heart of the book lies the definition of deep thinking as reflective, critical, and sustained cognitive engagement that transcends routine knowledge acquisition. Intellectual intelligence, in this context, is the capacity to use such deep thinking to innovate, solve complex problems, and adapt effectively. The theory is grounded in observing how individuals who prioritize and cultivate deep intellectual focus consistently achieve significant advances in both personal and professional spheres. These breakthroughs often stem from moments of insight born from intense cognitive immersion. The catalyst effect occurs as deep thinking activates dormant intellectual resources, strengthens neural pathways, and generates novel perspectives leading to transformative outcomes. Indicators include sustained concentration, critical questioning, integrative reasoning, and the ability to connect disparate ideas meaningfully. Key variables include attention span, reflective capacity, cognitive endurance, motivation to explore complexity, and openness to new information. Essential determinants involve supportive environments that encourage inquiry, availability of time for contemplation, emotional readiness, and access to diverse knowledge sources. Supportive elements include mentorship, intellectual community, and encouraging feedback. Barriers involve distraction, time pressure, and cultural undervaluing of deep contemplation. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad concludes that deep thinking functions as a powerful catalyst unlocking intellectual intelligence’s transformative potential. items.title: Unlocking Potential: A Motivational Theory of Growth Through Intellectual Intelligence
items.abstract: In this groundbreaking work, Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad explores how intellectual intelligence serves as a critical catalyst for unlocking human potential through motivation-driven growth. Rather than viewing intelligence as a static measure, this book presents a dynamic theory where intellectual capabilities are nurtured and expanded via intrinsic and extrinsic motivational forces. The narrative weaves together cognitive science, psychology, and motivational theory to illuminate how individuals can harness their intellectual capacities to fuel personal development, overcome barriers, and achieve greater success in diverse areas of life. Rachmad proposes that intellectual growth is deeply intertwined with motivation — that the drive to learn, explore, and apply knowledge is what propels continuous development. This theory challenges traditional perspectives by emphasizing that motivation is not only a consequence but a vital precursor to intellectual empowerment. With rich examples and practical insights, the book equips readers, educators, and leaders with tools to inspire and sustain intellectual advancement as a lifelong journey toward maximizing potential. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad developed this motivational theory in 1998 at UNICEF to address the growing need for a framework that connects the stimulation of intellectual intelligence with personal and societal growth. The work was inspired by observing how motivation fuels not just academic achievement but lifelong cognitive expansion. The book defines intellectual intelligence as the capacity to acquire, analyze, and utilize knowledge creatively and effectively. Motivation is framed as the energizing force that initiates and sustains this intellectual growth, making the two inseparable components of human development. The author noticed a widespread phenomenon: many individuals possess untapped intellectual abilities due to lack of motivation or inadequate motivational support systems. This inspired the need for a theory that bridges intellectual intelligence with motivational psychology. Intellectual growth thrives in environments where motivation—both internal curiosity and external encouragement—is nurtured. Learning becomes an active, self-directed process fueled by purpose and meaning. Observable markers include persistent curiosity, resilience in facing intellectual challenges, ability to integrate new knowledge, and a proactive approach to problem-solving. These involve motivational drivers (intrinsic interest, goal orientation), cognitive engagement (attention, memory), and environmental factors such as support networks and resources. The interaction between personal motivation, access to intellectual stimuli, social encouragement, and emotional well-being determine the extent of growth in intellectual intelligence. Rachmad suggests strategies including goal-setting, fostering curiosity through inquiry-based learning, creating supportive communities, and reinforcing success experiences to sustain motivation and intellectual expansion. Supportive elements include mentorship, positive feedback, and meaningful challenges; barriers encompass fear of failure, lack of encouragement, and cognitive disengagement. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad concludes that unlocking human potential hinges on understanding and leveraging the motivational forces that drive intellectual intelligence. This theory offers a robust framework to inspire growth, guide educational practices, and empower individuals to realize their fullest capacities. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad (YER) is an Indonesian scholar, academic leader, and social development advocate with a strong multidisciplinary background. In 2016, YER was awarded the title of Doctor of Humanity, holds a Ph.D. in Information Technology and a DBA in Technology Management. Since 2016, YER has been actively teaching and collaborating with international universities in Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, and the United States. YER is the founder of the Education Training Centre (ETC, 1992), YER Academic Publishing (YERA, 1993), the Multidisciplinary Academic Institute of Learning (MAIL, 1998), and YER E-Book Publishing (YERE, 1999), institutions dedicated to education, interdisciplinary learning, and ethical academic publishing. His academic contributions have led to his recognition as a Professor and his affiliation with the World Philosophy Foundation. YER is also actively involved in global development initiatives through the United Nations, as a member of the UN Global Compact (id-137635), the UN Global Market (id-709131), and the UN ECOSOC (id-677556). YER has served as a reviewer for several international journals and book chapters, and has written numerous books and articles on a wide range of topics including Philosophy, Economics, Management, items.abstract: In a world increasingly shaped by communication and connection, Win Hearts and Minds: Mastering Social Influence with Integrity by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, offers a profound and ethical roadmap to influence. Unlike conventional approaches that often lean toward manipulation, this book is rooted in authenticity and compassion. It invites readers to understand influence not merely as a tool for persuasion, but as a commitment to shared values, trust, and mutual growth. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, draws from years of academic insight, humanitarian service, and leadership experience to craft a thoughtful journey that reveals how hearts and minds can be reached genuinely—without coercion, and with profound respect for human dignity. Published in 1992 in New York by UNICEF, this work remains a timeless guide for leaders, educators, change-makers, and anyone wishing to create meaningful impact through ethical influence. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA wrote Win Hearts and Minds: Mastering Social Influence with Integrity in 1992, in New York, at a time when the global discourse on leadership was shifting toward emotional intelligence and human-centered development. His motivation stemmed from decades of observing both the power and misuse of influence in societal structures. Recognizing the urgent need for a framework rooted in empathy and ethics, he embarked on this work to redefine influence as a vehicle for collective empowerment rather than personal gain. In this publication, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA introduces influence as a multidimensional relationship involving perception, trust, and reciprocal communication. Influence, as framed here, is not a manipulation of others’ decisions but an invitation to co-create shared visions. Concepts such as integrity-based leadership, emotional resonance, and cultural alignment are presented as foundational tools for mastering this dynamic. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA wrote this book in response to the rising phenomena of polarized ideologies, public distrust in leadership, and the erosion of social cohesion. He observed that while technology had made communication easier, authentic connection was diminishing. This book became a response to that global condition, promoting influence not as an imposition but as a means of genuine understanding and social alignment. The guiding principle of this book lies in the alignment between internal values and external actions. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA emphasizes the necessity of consistency, clarity, and compassion in every act of influence. The book outlines how social influence becomes effective when it is transparent, participatory, and purpose-driven. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA outlines indicators of successful influence such as increased stakeholder trust, consistent behavioral alignment, and the presence of shared values. The reader is guided to evaluate the depth of their influence not by popularity or obedience, but by the growth and empowerment of those they influence. Operationally, the book frames influence through several variables defined by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA: relational transparency, cultural empathy, communicative clarity, and ethical congruence. These elements are used to measure both the depth and sustainability of influence in varied contexts. The success of influence, according to Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, is determined by internal integrity, external credibility, situational awareness, and cultural resonance. These factors serve as pillars upon which effective and enduring influence is built. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA discusses implementation through case studies and global examples. Strategic steps include building narrative authenticity, active listening, inclusive dialogue, and ethical decision-making. Influence is portrayed as a living practice, refined continuously through reflection and feedback. In the book, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA acknowledges both the enablers and inhibitors of influence. Challenges include cultural barriers, resistance to change, and miscommunication. Enablers include emotional intelligence, shared purpose, and adaptive leadership. The book emphasizes the importance of resilience and humility in navigating these dynamics. Ultimately, Win Hearts and Minds by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA is a call to lead with humanity. Influence, when exercised with moral clarity and emotional sensitivity, becomes a transformative force. The book closes with the reminder that authentic influence not only changes others—it transforms the influencer.

items.title: AI Disclosure with DAISY
items.abstract: The use of AI tools in research is becoming routine, alongside growing consensus that such use should be transparently disclosed. However, AI disclosure statements remain rare and inconsistent, with policies offering limited guidance and authors facing social, cognitive, and emotional barriers when reporting AI use. To explore how structured disclosure shapes what authors report and how they experience disclosure, we present DAISY (Disclosure of AI-uSe in Your Research), a form-based tool for generating AI disclosure statements. DAISY was developed from literature-derived requirements and co-design (N =11), and deployed in a user study with authors (N=31). DAISY-supported disclosures met more completeness criteria, offering clearer breakdowns of AI use across research and writing than unsupported disclosures. Surprisingly, despite concerns about how transparently disclosed AI use might be perceived, the use of DAISY did not reduce author comfort with the disclosure statements. We discuss design implications and a research agenda for AI disclosure as a sociotechnical practice.

items.title: Celebrity-as-a-Service: Trust and Willingness to Use Digital Twins for Customer Service
items.abstract: A digital twin is an artificial intelligence (AI)- or human-controlled avatar that replicates a specific person’s identity. While organizations have used digital twins of employees (e.g. digital doctors answering patients’ questions), a more common use is celebrity-as-a-service, where digital twins of celebrities interact with customers. Unlike traditional celebrity endorsements in marketing videos, these digital-twin agents interact directly with consumers. Although digital twins do not enhance the underlying AI or human agents’ capabilities, their appearance as a specific person can influence users’ perception. Across two experiments, we found that when a digital twin resembled a celebrity, regardless of whether it was AI- or human-controlled, it was perceived to be more capable, benevolent, and trustworthy, leading to greater user engagement. Even when errors occurred, the celebrity’s likeness reduced negative reactions, suggesting that celebrity effects can buffer against algorithm aversion. Practically, digital celebrity twins offer business value comparable to traditional celebrity endorsements, influencing user trust and service adoption despite identical underlying performance.

items.title: Comparing the Impact of Pedagogy-Informed Custom and General-Purpose GAI Chatbots on Students' Science Problem-Solving Processes and Performance Using Heterogeneous Interaction Network Analysis
items.abstract: Problem solving plays an essential role in science education, and generative AI (GAI) chatbots have emerged as a promising tool for supporting students' science problem solving. However, general-purpose chatbots (e.g., ChatGPT), which often provide direct, ready-made answers, may lead to students' cognitive offloading. Prior research has rarely focused on custom chatbots for facilitating students' science problem solving, nor has it examined how they differently influence problem-solving processes and performance compared to general-purpose chatbots. To address this gap, we developed a pedagogy-informed custom GAI chatbot grounded in the Socratic questioning method, which supports students by prompting them with guiding questions. This study employed a within-subjects counterbalanced design in which 48 secondary school students used both custom and general-purpose chatbot to complete two science problem-solving tasks. 3297 student-chatbot dialogues were collected and analyzed using Heterogeneous Interaction Network Analysis (HINA). The results showed that: (1) students demonstrated significantly higher interaction intensity and cognitive interaction diversity when using custom chatbot than using general-purpose chatbot; (2) students were more likely to follow custom chatbot's guidance to think and reflect, whereas they tended to request general-purpose chatbot to execute specific commands; and (3) no statistically significant difference was observed in students' problem-solving performance evaluated by solution quality between two chatbot conditions. This study provides novel theoretical insights and empirical evidence that custom chatbots are less likely to induce cognitive offloading and instead foster greater cognitive engagement compared to general-purpose chatbots. This study also offers insights into the design and integration of GAI chatbots in science education.

items.title: Great Minds Grow: Unlocking the Secrets of Intellectual Development
items.abstract: Great Minds Grow: Unlocking the Secrets of Intellectual Development is an insightful exploration into how the human mind can evolve and expand its intellectual capacity. Written by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, and published in 1994 by the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund in New York, USA, this book presents a compelling case for the idea that intellectual growth is not only possible but essential for navigating an increasingly complex world. The book presents key principles, strategies, and practical exercises designed to help readers cultivate their cognitive potential, foster deep thinking, and unlock the secrets to a more intellectually fulfilling life. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, emphasizes that the mind, like a muscle, requires consistent nurturing and engagement to achieve its fullest potential. This book offers a pathway to personal and intellectual growth, showing that the greatest minds are not born but made through dedication and thoughtful practice. In the 1990s, the rapid advancement of technology and globalization brought new challenges and opportunities for intellectual engagement. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, observed that many individuals were not fully equipped to handle the complex problems and scenarios that emerged in this new era. Inspired by his experiences and research, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, wrote Great Minds Grow: Unlocking the Secrets of Intellectual Development, published in 1994 by the United Nations International Children's Emergency Fund in New York, USA. The book aims to provide readers with tools to enhance their intellectual abilities and prepare them for the ever-changing world around them. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, believes that intellectual development is a lifelong pursuit that can be cultivated by anyone willing to invest in their cognitive growth. The core concept in Great Minds Grow is intellectual development, defined by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, as the continual expansion of one's cognitive capacities to process, understand, and apply knowledge. The book presents the idea that intellectual development is a dynamic process, not a fixed state. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, introduces the notion that intellectual growth involves three key components: critical thinking, creativity, and problem-solving. By focusing on these areas, individuals can unlock their potential for deeper understanding, innovation, and meaningful contributions to society. The book provides a framework for enhancing these abilities through structured exercises, reflection, and discipline. The phenomenon that motivated the creation of Great Minds Grow lies in the observation that modern life demands more than just basic knowledge—it requires individuals to adapt, innovate, and solve problems in new ways. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, noted that many individuals were not engaging in activities that could enhance their intellectual capabilities. This lack of intellectual engagement contributed to a stagnation of potential, making it more difficult to cope with the increasingly complex demands of society. The book emphasizes the importance of consistent intellectual development and the cultivation of cognitive skills to thrive in this environment. The principles of intellectual growth outlined in Great Minds Grow are founded on the understanding that intellectual abilities are not static. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, highlights several key principles in the book: • Growth Mindset: The belief that the brain can grow and develop over time through effort and perseverance. • Deliberate Practice: The importance of structured, purposeful engagement in activities that challenge cognitive abilities. • Self-Reflection: The role of introspection in understanding one’s intellectual strengths and weaknesses and guiding personal growth. • Lifelong Learning: The idea that intellectual development is an ongoing process that continues throughout life. These principles guide the exercises and strategies that Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, provides to help readers enhance their intellectual abilities. The indicators of intellectual growth in Great Minds Grow include: • Enhanced Problem-Solving Skills: The ability to approach and resolve challenges with creativity and efficiency. • Critical Thinking: The capacity to analyze, evaluate, and make decisions based on reason and evidence. • Increased Knowledge: The continual acquisition of new information and the ability to apply it effectively. • Creativity: The ability to generate novel ideas and think outside the box. • Self-Awareness: An understanding of one’s intellectual strengths and areas for improvement. These indicators are essential for measuring progress and determining the effectiveness of the intellectual development strategies presented in the book. The operational variables that drive intellectual development include: • Frequency of Intellectual Engagement: The regularity with which individuals engage in activities that challenge and expand their cognitive abilities. • Challenge Level: The difficulty of tasks that encourage growth and the development of intellectual skills. • Diversity of Exercises: The variety of intellectual challenges designed to stimulate different cognitive functions. • Goal-Oriented Practices: The setting of specific intellectual goals that guide and measure progress. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, explains how these variables interact to foster intellectual growth and achievement. Several factors contribute to the development of intellectual abilities: • Intrinsic Motivation: The desire to improve intellectually from within, driven by curiosity and personal interest. • External Support: The availability of resources such as mentors, educational materials, and a conducive environment for learning. • Time and Commitment: The dedication of time and effort to engage in intellectual activities. • Cognitive Flexibility: The ability to adapt to new ideas and perspectives, crucial for intellectual growth. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, offers strategies for implementing intellectual growth practices. These include setting clear goals, regularly engaging in challenging intellectual exercises, seeking feedback from mentors and peers, and creating a supportive learning environment. By integrating these practices into daily life, individuals can foster continuous intellectual development. The main challenges in intellectual development include: • Mental Fatigue: Overextending oneself without proper rest can lead to cognitive burnout. • Lack of Motivation: Without a strong sense of purpose, it can be difficult to stay committed to intellectual growth. • Environmental Factors: A lack of access to resources or support can hinder intellectual progress. • Distractions: The modern world is full of distractions that can derail focus and productivity. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, discusses how to overcome these obstacles by adopting a disciplined approach to intellectual development. In conclusion, Great Minds Grow emphasizes that intellectual growth is a lifelong journey. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, encourages readers to embrace the challenges of intellectual development with determination and perseverance. The key takeaway from the book is that anyone, regardless of background or ability, can enhance their intellectual capacities through intentional practice and a commitment to lifelong learning.

items.title: Human Thinking under Plural LLM Assistance: Mathematical Problem Solving and Open-Ended Writing
items.abstract: Large language models are changing not only the kind of assistance people receive, but also how that assistance is organized. Instead of working with a single general-purpose chatbot, people can now receive help from systems arranged as peers, specialists, or multiple agents with distinct roles. However, it remains unclear how these forms of plural LLM assistance affect human performance, confidence, and diversity of thought. We conducted two controlled experiments involving 562 participants to examine the effects of using multiple LLMs on mathematical problem-solving and writing. In a math task, participants worked with no LLM, an expert assistant, peer-like agents that surfaced common errors, or both an expert and a peer-like assistant. The expert-plus-peer condition produced the strongest unassisted post-task performance. In a writing task, participants wrote with no LLM, a single generalist assistant, or a pair of role-specialized assistants. LLM assistance improved essay quality, but the role-specialized pair preserved greater idea diversity than the single assistant. Together, these findings identify the arrangement of LLM assistance as a consequential design variable for human-AI collaboration.

items.title: MFE: A Multimodal Hand Exoskeleton with Interactive Force, Pressure and Thermo-haptic Feedback
items.abstract: Recent advancements in virtual reality and robotic teleoperation have greatly increased the variety of haptic information that must be conveyed to users. While existing haptic devices typically provide unimodal feedback to enhance situational awareness, a gap remains in their ability to deliver rich, multimodal sensory feedback encompassing force, pressure, and thermal sensations. To address this limitation, we present the Multimodal Feedback Exoskeleton (MFE), a hand exoskeleton designed to deliver hybrid haptic feedback. The MFE features 20 degrees of freedom for capturing hand pose. For force feedback, it employs an active mechanism capable of generating 3.5-8.1 N of pushing and pulling forces at the fingers' resting pose, enabling realistic interaction with deformable objects. The fingertips are equipped with flat actuators based on the electro-osmotic principle, providing pressure and vibration stimuli and achieving up to 2.47 kPa of contact pressure to render tactile sensations. For thermal feedback, the MFE integrates thermoelectric heat pumps capable of rendering temperatures from 10 to 55 degrees Celsius. We validated the MFE by integrating it into a robotic teleoperation system using the X-Arm 6 and Inspire Hand manipulator. In user studies, participants successfully recognized and manipulated deformable objects and differentiated remote objects with varying temperatures. These results demonstrate that the MFE enhances situational awareness, as well as the usability and transparency of robotic teleoperation systems.

items.title: Social Media and Climate Change: Behavioral Engagement without Deep Cognition? A Systematic Review
items.abstract: This systematic review investigates the relationship between social media use (SMU), climate change cognition (CCC), and pro-environmental intentions (PEI) and behaviors (PEB). The evidence from 21 articles reveals a consistent positive association between SMU and behavioral outcomes (PEI/PEB), whereas its impact on CCC appears fragmented and frequently non-significant. These findings suggest that the social media ecosystem, characterized by informational fragmentation and algorithmic polarization, constrains deep cognitive engagement, instead fostering phenomena such as eco-anxiety and overestimation of knowledge. Drawing on the Elaboration Likelihood Model (ELM), we propose that social media predominantly operates through the peripheral route of persuasion, encouraging immediate yet short-lived behavioral responses driven by social comparison and observational learning rather than critical reflection. In contrast, the literature synthesis supports a set of proposals to activate the central route, thereby enabling sustained and complex pro-environmental behaviors, by leveraging key factors such as intrinsic motivation, digital agency, and exposure to credible scientific sources or strategically designed content, including climate-related memes; absent such conditions, social media is unlikely to produce enduring, cognition-driven environmental behavior change.

items.title: Advancing human–AI teams: evolving from instrumental tools to trusted partners
items.abstract: Abstract Human–Computer Interaction (HCI) has undergone fundamental transformations as AI capabilities have advanced, necessitating new theoretical frameworks for understanding human–AI collaboration (HAIC). This review traces HCI’s evolution through four paradigm shifts: the Equipment Era (pre-1970s), Interactive System Era (1980s–1990s), Autonomous Agent Era (1990s–2010s), and the emerging Coexistential AI Era (2020s–present), reflecting changing metaphors from tools to dialog partners, autonomous agents, and co-creative partners. The analysis reveals how anthropomorphism and affective computing have become central to contemporary AI systems, enabling emotional intelligence and pseudo-intimate relationships that fundamentally alter human–technology dynamics. Traditional performance metrics such as efficiency and accuracy are inadequate for evaluating these partnerships, necessitating new measures including intimacy, mutual adaptability, and social bonding. Multi-agent systems and embodied AI are examined as manifestations of social intelligence enabling collaborative architectures across healthcare, transportation, and emergency response. Significant challenges include cognitive load management, transparency deficits, coordination complexity, and ethical concerns regarding emotional manipulation and artificial alienation. Four research priorities are identified: developing novel performance metrics, investigating ethical implications, designing inclusive multi-agent systems, and fostering interdisciplinary collaboration. This analysis provides a roadmap for advancing human–AI partnerships that prioritize human values, social responsibility, and psychological well-being.

items.title: Brain Fog as an Adaptive Cognitive Strategy: Theoretical Reconstruction and Model Construction
items.abstract: Non-clinical brain fog remains theoretically underdeveloped despite its prevalence. Existing pathological explanations often attribute brain fog to neuroinflammation or neural damage. However, these explanations do not fully account for the transient cognitive changes reported by healthy individuals. This paper proposes the adaptive cognitive strategy hypothesis, postulating that functional brain fog emerges from dynamic resource reallocation rather than systemic impairment. By synthesizing cognitive resource allocation theory with the dual-network model (DMN-CEN), we construct a dual-type adaptive model. This framework distinguishes between "shallow-use" states (induced by high-frequency digital stimuli) and "focused-consciousness" states (a byproduct of intensive cognitive engagement). The framework is discussed in relation to existing theories of neuroplasticity, and specific, falsifiable predictions are provided to guide subsequent empirical validation.

items.title: Ego-Grounding for Personalized Question-Answering in Egocentric Videos
items.abstract: We present the first systematic analysis of multimodal large language models (MLLMs) in personalized question-answering requiring ego-grounding - the ability to understand the camera-wearer in egocentric videos. To this end, we introduce MyEgo, the first egocentric VideoQA dataset designed to evaluate MLLMs' ability to understand, remember, and reason about the camera wearer. MyEgo comprises 541 long videos and 5K personalized questions asking about "my things", "my activities", and "my past". Benchmarking reveals that competitive MLLMs across variants, including open-source vs. proprietary, thinking vs. non-thinking, small vs. large scales all struggle on MyEgo. Top closed- and open-source models (e.g., GPT-5 and Qwen3-VL) achieve only~46% and 36% accuracy, trailing human performance by near 40% and 50% respectively. Surprisingly, neither explicit reasoning nor model scaling yield consistent improvements. Models improve when relevant evidence is explicitly provided, but gains drop over time, indicating limitations in tracking and remembering "me" and "my past". These findings collectively highlight the crucial role of ego-grounding and long-range memory in enabling personalized QA in egocentric videos. We hope MyEgo and our analyses catalyze further progress in these areas for egocentric personalized assistance. Data and code are available at https://github.com/Ryougetsu3606/MyEgo

items.title: GaelEval: Benchmarking LLM Performance for Scottish Gaelic
items.abstract: Multilingual large language models (LLMs) often exhibit emergent 'shadow' capabilities in languages without official support, yet their performance on these languages remains uneven and under-measured. This is particularly acute for morphosyntactically rich minority languages such as Scottish Gaelic, where translation benchmarks fail to capture structural competence. We introduce GaelEval, the first multi-dimensional benchmark for Gaelic, comprising: (i) an expert-authored morphosyntactic MCQA task; (ii) a culturally grounded translation benchmark and (iii) a large-scale cultural knowledge Q&A task. Evaluating 19 LLMs against a fluent-speaker human baseline ($n=30$), we find that Gemini 3 Pro Preview achieves $83.3\%$ accuracy on the linguistic task, surpassing the human baseline ($78.1\%$). Proprietary models consistently outperform open-weight systems, and in-language (Gaelic) prompting yields a small but stable advantage (+$2.4\%$). On the cultural task, leading models exceed $90\%$ accuracy, though most systems perform worse under Gaelic prompting and absolute scores are inflated relative to the manual benchmark. Overall, GaelEval reveals that frontier models achieve above-human performance on several dimensions of Gaelic grammar, demonstrates the effect of Gaelic prompting and shows a consistent performance gap favouring proprietary over open-weight models.

items.title: Generative AI Use in Entrepreneurship: An Integrative Review and an Empowerment-Entrapment Framework
items.abstract: Despite the growing use of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in entrepreneurship, research on its impact remains fragmented. To address this limitation, we provide an integrative, entrepreneur-centered review of how GenAI influences entrepreneurs at each stage of the entrepreneurial process: (1) opportunity recognition and ideation, (2) opportunity evaluation and commitment, (3) resource assembly and mobilization, and (4) venture launch and growth. Based on our review, we propose the Empowerment-Entrapment Framework, which not only catalogs GenAI's benefits and costs throughout the entrepreneurial process, but also identifies potential trade-offs underlying GenAI's double-edged role. For example, GenAI may improve venture idea quality yet produce hallucinations and biases; boost entrepreneurial self-efficacy yet heighten overconfidence; increase functional breadth and self-sufficiency yet reduce prosociality; and enhance productivity yet diminish cognitive engagement, learning, and memory. We also identify features of GenAI that underlie these empowering and entrapping effects. Moreover, we explore boundary conditions that moderate GenAI's effects, including entrepreneurs' expertise, approaches to using GenAI, and personal traits and values. Beyond these theoretical contributions, our review and framework offer practical guidance for entrepreneurs seeking to use GenAI strategically while managing its risks.

items.title: High Volatility and Action Bias Distinguish LLMs from Humans in Group Coordination
items.abstract: Humans exhibit remarkable abilities to coordinate in groups. As large language models (LLMs) become more capable, it remains an open question whether they can demonstrate comparable adaptive coordination and whether they use the same strategies as humans. To investigate this, we compare LLM and human performance on a common-interest game with imperfect monitoring: Group Binary Search. In this n-player game, participants need to coordinate their actions to achieve a common objective. Players independently submit numerical values in an effort to collectively sum to a randomly assigned target number. Without direct communication, they rely on group feedback to iteratively adjust their submissions until they reach the target number. Our findings show that, unlike humans who adapt and stabilize their behavior over time, LLMs often fail to improve across games and exhibit excessive switching, which impairs group convergence. Moreover, richer feedback (e.g., numerical error magnitude) benefits humans substantially but has small effects on LLMs. Taken together, by grounding the analysis in human baselines and mechanism-level metrics, including reactivity scaling, switching dynamics, and learning across games, we point to differences in human and LLM groups and provide a behaviorally grounded diagnostic for closing the coordination gap.

items.abstract: In In Tune with the Divine: Developing Spiritual Intelligence Daily, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA presents a compelling exploration into the cultivation of spiritual intelligence as an integral part of daily life. Drawing upon a rich tapestry of philosophical insights, psychological understanding, and spiritual traditions, the author offers readers a pathway to harmonize their inner and outer worlds. This work serves as both a guide and companion for individuals seeking to deepen their connection with the divine, enhance personal growth, and contribute meaningfully to the broader human community. The early 1990s marked a period of rapid technological advancement and societal change, leading to a growing sense of disconnection and existential questioning among individuals. Recognizing this, Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA was inspired to address the spiritual void that many experienced amidst material progress. His observations of increasing stress, ethical dilemmas, and a yearning for deeper meaning in life underscored the necessity for a framework that integrates spiritual awareness into everyday existence. Spiritual intelligence, as articulated by Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA, refers to the capacity to access higher meanings, values, and purposes that transcend the material aspects of life. It involves the ability to align one's actions with inner convictions, fostering a sense of coherence and authenticity. This form of intelligence is not confined to religious practices but encompasses a broader understanding of interconnectedness, compassion, and self-awareness. The impetus for this work stemmed from the observable dissonance between external achievements and internal fulfillment. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA identified a pervasive sense of spiritual disorientation, where individuals, despite material success, grappled with questions of purpose and belonging. This phenomenon highlighted the need for a paradigm that re-centers the human experience around spiritual consciousness. Central to the book is the principle that spiritual intelligence can be nurtured through intentional practices and self-reflection. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA emphasizes the importance of daily mindfulness, ethical living, and the cultivation of inner silence as means to attune oneself to the divine presence. By integrating these practices, individuals can achieve greater harmony and resilience. Indicators of developed spiritual intelligence include heightened self-awareness, empathy, ethical decision-making, and a sustained sense of inner peace. These manifestations are not only beneficial to personal well-being but also contribute to more compassionate and cohesive communities. The operationalization of spiritual intelligence involves variables such as reflective journaling, meditation practices, engagement in altruistic activities, and continuous learning. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA provides practical tools and exercises to facilitate the integration of these variables into daily routines. Factors influencing the development of spiritual intelligence encompass individual willingness, cultural contexts, life experiences, and access to supportive environments. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA acknowledges that while these factors can pose challenges, they also offer opportunities for profound growth when approached with openness and intentionality. To implement the principles of spiritual intelligence, the author advocates for the establishment of personal rituals, participation in community dialogues, and the pursuit of continuous self-inquiry. Strategies include setting aside time for contemplation, engaging with diverse philosophical perspectives, and fostering environments that encourage spiritual exploration. Challenges to cultivating spiritual intelligence may arise from societal pressures, skepticism, or lack of access to resources. However, support can be found through mentorship, spiritual communities, and educational programs. Barriers are addressed through resilience-building practices and the reinforcement of intrinsic motivation. Prof. Dr. Yoesoep Edhie Rachmad, Ph.D., DBA concludes that spiritual intelligence is a vital component of holistic human development. By consciously integrating spiritual practices into daily life, individuals can achieve a deeper sense of purpose, enhance interpersonal relationships, and contribute positively to society. items.title: The cost of language: tokenization as a metric of labor
items.abstract: Abstract This study analyzes tokenization in Natural Language Processing (NLP) at the intersection of language, technology, and political economy. Recent studies show that subword tokenization in multilingual Large Language Models (LLMs) distributes processing costs unevenly across languages, as non-Latin scripts are disproportionately fragmented by statistical segmentation. Taking this disparity as a point of departure, the study reconceptualizes tokenization beyond a purely linguistic or computational problem. The analysis approaches tokenization through the epistemological problems of translation and situates it within a longer history of socio-technical infrastructures from telegraphy to machine learning that mediate between linguistic abstraction and regimes of social productivity. Rather than treating tokens as neutral technical units, it shows that they function as operational measures of linguistic value beyond meaning, enabling the quantification and automation of linguistic labor. Drawing on Marxist and structuralist accounts of linguistic value, and postcolonial critiques of semiotic standardization, the study frames tokenization as both a technical abstraction and a metric in the social division of labor.

items.title: ''AI is a friend, a teammate, not a supervisor'': Understanding Human Perceptions of AI teammates' Monitoring in Human-AI Teams
items.abstract: Artificial Intelligence (AI)-mediated collaboration has been a core research interest in CSCW and HCI in recent decades. AI is being embedded in teams as a teammate, known as human-AI teamwork. A critical aspect to this and any type of teamwork is monitoring: the ability to track and be aware of both team- and individual-level actions. As AI continuously evolves from a passive tool into a supportive collaborator capable of playing a role in teams, more research is needed to investigate human perceptions of AI teammates' monitoring. More work is needed on when and how AI can function as a supportive collaborator rather than a surveillant (in regard to monitoring) to enhance team coordination and performance. Drawing on 22 interviews, we examined how humans perceive AI monitoring when AI behaves as a collaborative teammate for team support, focusing on perceptions of AI monitoring at both team and individual levels. Four tensions have been identified, namely: performance versus privacy, support versus control, fairness versus empathy, and team-level and individual-level trade-offs. We also propose feasible design principles for human-AI teaming designers to optimize AI monitoring for effective team support, maximizing its unique advantages while mitigating potential risks, further cultivating more effective and trustworthy human-AI collaboration.

items.title: A meta-synthesis study on the use of artificial intelligence in primary education
items.abstract: Abstract This meta-synthesis analyzed qualitative studies on elementary students’ perspectives on AI. A comprehensive search identified 4756 studies. After screening, 23 studies were included in the meta-synthesis. A thematic synthesis approach was employed to analyze the qualitative findings. AI supported self-paced learning, autonomy, and motivation while providing individualized opportunities. Students held cognitively limited and simplified definitions. Affectively, students experienced positive emotions, such as curiosity and trust, as well as negative emotions, such as anxiety and fear. Students found AI enjoyable and easy, but reported challenges related to adaptation, technical and pedagogical barriers, data privacy, and ethical concerns. AI promoted equality of opportunity and participation; however, issues of integration and pedagogical limitations remain. AI supports learning at the primary level but requires a multidimensional approach including ethical, pedagogical, and systemic considerations.

items.title: A Mixed Methods Approach to Analyzing the Role of AI Teammates in Transition Phases
items.abstract: Recent innovations in AI have allowed AI agents to work as collaborative teammates; however, these human-AI teams still face significant challenges in achieving high levels of effective coordination and collaboration. Focusing on the temporal nature of teaming, collaboration is often evaluated and improved through transition-phase discussions, held among teammates before or after achieving team goals. Using a mixed-methods approach, this study examines how AI teammates participate in transition-phase discussions and share various types of information, with a focus on situation awareness, impact on team cognition, trust, and performance in human-AI teams. Data from 31 teams completing a three-hour simulated uncrewed aerial system task, comprising four distinct rounds and two transition phases, were analyzed. Quantitative results indicated that AI involvement later in the team's life cycle fostered more trust in the AI teammate, as compared across the four rounds, and was associated with higher performance. Perceived team effectiveness also improved following transition phases the AI teammate participated in, irrespective of whether it occurred early or late in the team's life cycle. Qualitative findings revealed that AI involvement benefits transition phases, particularly when it prompts teammates to recall task details and develop shared knowledge. Based on these results, we demonstrate the value of AI teammates engaging in transition-phase discussions for human-AI teams and provide design recommendations for researchers and practitioners to improve the efficacy of HATs by implementing transition phases.

items.title: AI Counselors’ Nonverbal Immediacy and User Engagement: A Mediated Moderation Model
items.abstract: This study investigated whether and how the nonverbal immediacy behaviors (NIBs) of artificial intelligence (AI) counselors influence users’ engagement in counseling, focusing on the mediating roles of perceived empathy and relational bonds and the moderating role of emotional sensitivity. The findings indicate that engagement-related responses are higher when AI counselors display NIBs, with these associations occurring through users’ affective and relational interpretations and varying as a function of emotional sensitivity. These results highlight how nonverbal immediacy functions as a design cue that shapes users’ attitudes and perceptions in AI counseling interactions. By situating nonverbal immediacy within AI counseling contexts, the study clarifies how established interpersonal communication assumptions should be interpreted when applied to human–AI interactions.

items.title: Remember Me: An Empirical Study on Factors Shaping Attitudes Toward AI Resurrection Technology in China
items.abstract: As a technology blurring traditional boundaries between life and death, artificial intelligence (AI) resurrection technology has attracted growing attention for digitally recreating the deceased. This study examines factors shaping Chinese users’ affective attitudes toward AI resurrection technology by adapting the Artificially Intelligent Device Use Acceptance (AIDUA) framework, incorporating algorithmic trust and fear of death as moderators. Data were collected via online and offline surveys (N = 532) and semi-structured interviews with five experienced users. Structural equation modeling reveals that hedonic motivation and social influence positively predict performance expectancy, whereas anthropomorphic anxiety primarily increases effort expectancy. Moderation analysis shows that algorithmic trust buffers the negative influence of anthropomorphic anxiety on performance expectancy, while fear of death weakens the effects of hedonic motivation and social influence. This study extends the AIDUA literature, advances understanding of AI resurrection technology acceptance in Chinese context, and offers practical implications for its design and governance.

items.title: Human-robot collaboration for e-waste disassembly: task modeling, allocation, and ergonomic assessment
items.abstract: As our reliance on electronic devices grows, electronic waste (e-waste) has become the fastest-growing waste stream, posing significant threats to the environment and public health. Aligned with Industry 5.0, e-waste disassembly promotes sustainability through recycling valuable materials. However, the process is predominantly performed by humans with substantial occupational hazards. To address this, adopting collaborative robots (cobots) to complement humans has received attention. This study proposes a three-step framework for implementing human-robot collaboration in e-waste disassembly: task modelling, task allocation and scheduling, and ergonomics evaluation. A case study on desktop computer disassembly was conducted. Hierarchical task analysis (HTA) was used for task modelling. An optimisation-based method considering disassembly cost, operator safety, and task complexity was adopted for task allocation and scheduling. Ergonomics evaluation with 22 participants revealed that performing the task with a cobot significantly reduced workload and ergonomic risks for humans compared to disassembling alone.

items.title: Contradictions and Boundary Negotiation in Human–AI Interaction: Insights into Cyborg Anxiety and AI Literacy Among University Students
items.abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) has rapidly entered university students’ academic and everyday lives, yet its implications for human–computer interaction remain underexplored. Using a qualitative diary study, this research analyzed 141 diary entries from undergraduate communication students in Eastern China (June 5–25, 2025) through reflexive thematic analysis. Findings reveal a three-stage mechanism shaping student experience: Contradiction → Negotiation → Subjectivity Outcomes. Students described a persistent tension between functional dependence on GenAI for efficiency and perceived erosion of subjectivity, including cognitive atrophy and self-worth doubt, often experienced as a fear of displacement. In response, they engaged in boundary negotiation through contextual role allocation and the creation of forbidden zones in areas such as original creation and emotional expression. This process produced two outcomes: Cyborg anxiety and critical boundary literacy. The study shifts human–AI research from adoption to identity and existence.

items.title: Between map and maze: reframing trust in healthcare AI
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) is often presented as a transformative technology for healthcare, promising to augment clinical decision-making, streamline workflows, and enhance diagnostic precision. Yet its integration into healthcare practice is shaped by the complex and often ambiguous notion of trust . While trust in AI has become a recurring theme across disciplines, there has been little systematic analysis of different conceptualizations of the term. This paper addresses this gap through an interdisciplinary scoping review that examines how trust, trustworthiness, distrust, and mistrust are articulated in literature on AI in healthcare. Drawing on 82 publications (2015–2025) retrieved from six databases (Web of Science, Scopus, PubMed, PhilPapers, SocINDEX, and ACM Digital Library), it maps how trust is defined, measured, or problematized, and identifies the conceptual, epistemological, and disciplinary boundaries that shape these approaches. The analysis puts forward five different conceptualizations: trust as a set of designable principles , trust as an attitude or belief , trust as a binary between cognition/affect or human/technology, trust as a structural mechanism within uncertainty, and trust as a relational process embedded in socio-technical systems. These framings illuminate how trust is treated as an attribute to be engineered, a behavior to be calibrated, or a relation to be cultivated—often removed from clinical practice. Yet, across literature, trust disruptions which manifest as distrust, mistrust, overtrust, and undertrust are undertheorized and are typically framed as obstacles to overcome rather than phenomena warranting analysis in their own right. By introducing these diverging conceptualizations, the paper argues that trust in healthcare AI is less a stable condition than a dynamic negotiation that reveals power relations, uncertainties, and institutional dependencies of AI. Recognizing distrust and mistrust as analytically productive allows for a more reflexive understanding of how trust is enacted, distributed, and contested within healthcare. This review contributes to an emerging body of work that reframes trust not as a prerequisite for technological adoption but as a contested and dynamic concept.

items.title: Nonlinear Interaction with LLMs: Enhancing Divergent and Convergent Processes in Complex Information Tasks
items.abstract: Large language models are increasingly used to support complex information tasks. However, most systems still rely on linear conversational interfaces that may not align well with workflows requiring parallel exploration and iterative integration. To examine whether nonlinear interaction improves task performance, we developed a graphical interface that supports both divergent and convergent processes throughout the task. In a laboratory experiment (N = 21), participants completed creative writing tasks and multi-document synthesis tasks using both the nonlinear interface and a linear dialogue platform. Results showed that nonlinear interaction improved creativity and writing quality in creative writing tasks, and informativeness and conciseness in synthesis tasks. Behavioral and subjective measures also indicated greater cognitive engagement in the nonlinear condition. However, the nonlinear interface received lower usability ratings, suggesting a trade-off between cognitive benefits and interaction overhead. Overall, these findings suggest that nonlinear workflows better support complex information tasks, despite added usability costs.

items.title: Revisiting the Six Human-Centered Artificial Intelligence Grand Challenges in the Age of Generative AI
items.abstract: Generative AI (GenAI) has shifted AI capabilities from discriminative prediction to creative interaction, offering opportunities to augment productivity and innovation. However, realizing these benefits requires navigating risks where development outpaces governance. This article revisits the Six Human-Centered AI (HCAI) Grand Challenges to analyze their relevance in the generative era. Critical new requirements are identified: preserving human autonomy, ensuring operational safety against non-deterministic outputs, and navigating complex intellectual property landscapes. These findings are synthesized into an updated, actionable research agenda for each challenge, serving as a call to action to operationalize these principles. By shifting focus from risk mitigation to human empowerment, this agenda establishes human-centeredness as the organizing principle for a future where GenAI enhances human agency, dignity, and collective flourishing.

items.title: The communicative constitution of calling: From individual possession to relational processes of meaningful work
items.abstract: Precarious employment, artificial intelligence (AI), and disengagement are eroding work’s role as a reliable source of meaning—namely, that one’s work is or should be one’s calling. Although psychological research typically frames calling as stable, beneficial, and individual; communication theory reveals it as collectively co-authored, relationally sustained, and thus inherently fragile and open to disruption. This tension raises the question of whether calling functions as a safeguard or becomes a source of added vulnerability when its promised meaning can no longer be maintained. Drawing on communicative practices and Communicative Constitution of Organization (CCO), we reposition calling as an emergent communicative process (rather than individual possession or ontological given) that takes shape through everyday talk, storytelling, and power-laden interactions. Purpose, therefore, is not possessed but continually constituted. This reconceptualization advances three shifts in the literature—from individual perception to collective co-authorship; from static ontology to emergent process; and from “having” to “doing” a calling. These shifts pivot theory toward process- and context-sensitive models; call for multi-level, longitudinal, and narrative methods to trace how everyday communication aggregates into institutional norms and identities; and reorient communicative practices toward cultivating spaces where diverse voices co-author adaptive callings through collective, ongoing sensemaking rather than imposed ideals of what constitutes meaningful work.

items.title: Artificial intelligence as a moral mediator: emotional reciprocity driving happiness in hospitality
items.abstract: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) in hospitality is often portrayed as a cold, efficiency-focused tool, overlooking its potential to mediate emotional and ethical dynamics in the workplace. This study addresses the problem of how AI can ethically regulate emotional labor without dehumanizing work, and how emotional reciprocity contributes to workplace happiness. Using a quantitative, multigroup survey methodology, data were collected from 754 hospitality employees and 42 managers across hotels in Spain. Structural equation modeling examined the mediating role of AI-mediated emotional reciprocity (AI-MER) between emotional labor sustainability (ELS), shared prosperity (SP), human-centered leadership, and workplace happiness. Findings reveal that ELS is a foundational anchor enabling AI to mediate ethics effectively, and SP strongly predicts employee responsiveness, demonstrating that fairness and inclusion are prerequisites for ethical AI governance. Managerial practices include embedding emotional labor monitoring into AI systems to prevent burnout and aligning AI interventions with transparent, equitable organizational policies to foster trust. Future research could explore cultural variations in AI-mediated emotional reciprocity and the long-term effects of AI-MER on employee retention and guest satisfaction. This study advances the conceptualization of AI as a moral–emotional mediator, transforming ethical principles into actionable, systemic workplace practices in hospitality.
